request.query: Finitely supported functions taking values in sets of bounded diameter: coefficientwise subtraction stays in difference sets, and subtraction of distinct functions is nonzero

content.text:
{
  "items": [
    {
      "formal_name": "DFinsupp.neLocus_sub_left",
      "informal_name": "Subtraction Preserves neLocus Equality",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {α : Type u_1} {N : α → Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : (a : α) → DecidableEq (N a)]\n  [inst_2 : (a : α) → AddGroup (N a)] (f g₁ g₂ : Π₀ (a : α), N a), (f - g₁).neLocus (f - g₂) = g₁.neLocus g₂",
      "informal_description": "For dependent finite support functions $f, g_1, g_2$ with values in additive groups, the set of indices where $f - g_1$ and $f - g_2$ differ equals the set of indices where $g_1$ and $g_2$ differ. Symbolically, $\\text{neLocus}(f - g_1, f - g_2) = \\text{neLocus}(g_1, g_2)$.",

    },
    {
      "formal_name": "Finsupp.neLocus_sub_left",
      "informal_name": "Equality of Difference Loci under Subtraction",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {α : Type u_1} {N : Type u_3} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : DecidableEq N] [inst_2 : AddGroup N]\n  (f g₁ g₂ : α →₀ N), (f - g₁).neLocus (f - g₂) = g₁.neLocus g₂",
      "informal_description": "For finite support functions $f, g_1, g_2 : \\alpha \\to_0 G$, the set of points where $f - g_1$ and $f - g_2$ differ is equal to the set of points where $g_1$ and $g_2$ differ, i.e., $\\mathrm{neLocus}(f - g_1, f - g_2) = \\mathrm{neLocus}(g_1, g_2)$.",
      "path": "Mathlib.Data.Finsupp.NeLocus"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "DFinsupp.neLocus_sub_right",
      "informal_name": "Invariance of Locus of Inequality Under Common Subtraction in Dependent Finite Support Functions",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {α : Type u_1} {N : α → Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : (a : α) → DecidableEq (N a)]\n  [inst_2 : (a : α) → AddGroup (N a)] (f₁ f₂ g : Π₀ (a : α), N a), (f₁ - g).neLocus (f₂ - g) = f₁.neLocus f₂",
      "informal_description": "For any dependent finite support functions $f₁, f₂, g$ with values in additive groups, the set of indices where $f₁ - g$ differs from $f₂ - g$ coincides with the set of indices where $f₁$ differs from $f₂$, i.e., $\\text{neLocus}(f₁ - g, f₂ - g) = \\text{neLocus}(f₁, f₂)$.",
      "path": "Mathlib.Data.DFinsupp.NeLocus"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "DFinsupp.neLocus_self_sub_left",
      "informal_name": "\\text{neLocus}(f - g, f) = \\text{support}(g)",

      "type": "∀ {α : Type u_1} {N : α → Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : (a : α) → DecidableEq (N a)]\n  [inst_2 : (a : α) → AddGroup (N a)] (f g : Π₀ (a : α), N a), (f - g).neLocus f = g.support",
      "informal_description": "The set of indices where the component-wise subtraction of $ g $ from $ f $ differs from $ f $ is equal to the support of $ g $.",

    },
    {
      "formal_name": "Finsupp.neLocus",
      "informal_name": "Locus of Points Where Finite Support Functions Differ",

      "type": "{α : Type u_1} → {N : Type u_3} → [DecidableEq α] → [DecidableEq N] → [inst : Zero N] → (α →₀ N) → (α →₀ N) → Finset α",

      "formal_name": "Finsupp.neLocus_sub_right",

      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {α : Type u_1} {N : Type u_3} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : DecidableEq N] [inst_2 : AddGroup N]\n  (f₁ f₂ g : α →₀ N), (f₁ - g).neLocus (f₂ - g) = f₁.neLocus f₂",
      "informal_description": "For finite support functions $f_1, f_2, g$, the set of points where $f_1 - g$ and $f_2 - g$ differ is equal to the set of points where $f_1$ and $f_2$ differ, i.e., $\\{x \\mid (f_1 - g)(x) \\neq (f_2 - g)(x)\\} = \\{x \\mid f_1(x) \\neq f_2(x)\\}$.",

items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {N : α → Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : (a : α) → DecidableEq (N a)]
  [inst_2 : (a : α) → AddGroup (N a)] (f g₁ g₂ : Π₀ (a : α), N a), (f - g₁).neLocus (f - g₂) = g₁.neLocus g₂
items.informal_description: For dependent finite support functions $f, g_1, g_2$ with values in additive groups, the set of indices where $f - g_1$ and $f - g_2$ differ equals the set of indices where $g_1$ and $g_2$ differ. Symbolically, $\text{neLocus}(f - g_1, f - g_2) = \text{neLocus}(g_1, g_2)$.
